title: Where to start ?
author: Hell_noki
selftext:
Hello everyone ! 

I am a developer that never used AI in a project, and I wondered where to start... I have some pretty specific needs, though :   
  
\- I don't want to become a professional prompter. I'm still a developer and I really like to write code/organize my project/make my systems myself, what I would like is an assistant that can write scripts **based on what I already made**. For instance, I'm using Godot for my game, and I have different scripts for different Effects already written ; speeding up the process of creating new Effects by AI sounds good since the whole system is already existent. Asking to build a whole game is a no-no.  
  
\- How do I organize myself with Git ? I guess the safest way to have an AI do something is to have it work in its branch, one commit at a time, but does that mean I have to have an external repository ? Like, I think I can't have my Git project stored locally, working on a branch AND having an AI working on another branch, can I ?

\- I'm not even sure I'll like to work assisted by an AI and I'm in a bit of a financial slump right now, are free plans worth the effort or do I really have to pay a subscription to try it out ? 

\- And... Where the hell do I start ?! There's like 100.000 models spread between 10 companies, how do I choose ? What do I have to install ? I guess an IDE module (I'm using VSCode) ? Or is the traditional way to work with AI is the good ol' copy/paste back and forth in a chat window ?

comments.author: Rizabekus
comments.body: Claude pro 20 dollars. Try opus 5.5, you will be amazed by what it does

replies.author: Hell_noki
replies.body: Thanks for the advice ! I'm a bit confused by their pricing page, with your subscription you get tokens for the Opus API ? Like when using the chatbot you can chose the model and it deduces your uses based on it ?

replies.author: Rizabekus
replies.body:
From how i understood Claude API is different from Claude code. If you are planning to use AI locally(claude code) you will be given weekly and 5h limits. weekly limits refresh every week and 5h refresh every 5h. Also there is option  "Usage credits" ->(Turn on usage credits to keep using Claude if you hit a plan limit. Credits are used only after you reach your plan limit. They don’t raise the limit. [Learn more](https://support.claude.com/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans)). By default it is disabled.   
Yes you can choose model in chatbot. limits of chatbot and claude code are connected.

replies.author: Hell_noki
replies.body: Thanks a bunch, that clarifies things :)

replies.author: Hell_noki
replies.body: The tightest the better. I just want to try at first, I'm not even sure I'll like AI assisted dev

replies.author: daddy_reloaded
replies.body:
Not sure how to reply then.
For a little try, the best option would be either codex or Claude $20 plan. But this will be a very short try. One day try I think (I don't know today how far you can go with the starter plans).

If you want to make a more comprehensive try, then I would suggest then 100$ plan from codex. You will get more usage compared to Claude but still have excellent experience. 

But I must warn you, ai assisted coding is becoming less and less useful. I am coding since 2000's and nothing can beat the latest LLM in terms of productivity. You can still advise and try to control the architecture but even that it is becoming less and less useful. 

And at one point, you are going to use llm full time and will need a higher plan, at least a max one.

replies.author: Hell_noki
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback !  
   
About one day for $20 hurts a bit to read, and I don't know if I want to spend $100 in this... 

I know AIs are getting more and more efficient, and that my work is destined to disappear, but I'm not looking only for a result. I don't want to think only about productivity for my own project, if I don't take pleasure in what I am doing it loses a lot of meaning, so I have to balance everything out. As I said, I like to write code, I'm not looking for something to replace me, I'm looking for something to assist me through the most repetitive tasks.

replies.author: Hell_noki
replies.body: Thanks ! I was missing the MCP part
